text:
Cole Hutson won it for Washington 74 seconds into overtime, taking a feed from Alex Ovechkin and Dylan Strome and finishing a game the Capitals had no real claim to. Hutson, a second-round pick (43rd overall) in 2024 who played at Boston University last season, also set up Pierre-Luc Dubois's tying goal in the third period.

Our numbers say Ottawa was the better team. We estimate expected goals, the quality of each team's chances, at 2.85 for OTT and 2.12 for WSH. Our "deserved to win" figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave the Senators 63 percent. Ottawa piled up 70 shot attempts to 40 and won 41 of 63 faceoffs. The second period was the clearest stretch: OTT out-chanced WSH 1.61 to 0.73 and got goals from Ridly Greig and Hayden Hodgson to flip a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Washington's first goal was a 3 percent chance, Matt Roy's slap shot 35 seconds in.

Logan Thompson is why it stayed close. He stopped 24 of 26 shots and finished 0.85 goals saved above expected, meaning he gave his team nearly one more goal of help than an average goalie would on those chances. Washington also blocked 25 shots to Ottawa's nine. Samuel Ersson faced just 17 shots and allowed three, which cost him 0.88 goals against expectation. Neither side scored on the power play (WSH 0 for 4, OTT 0 for 3). Ottawa took the loss, and Thomas Chabot's two assists went for nothing.
